card.title: NIGHT PATROL
card.text: Draw 2 cards. Then choose a card in hand and put it on top of your deck.
card.flavorText: During WWII, the US Navy relied on several types of small, fast vessels for night patrols, especially in the Pacific and around contested coastal areas. The most famous were PT boats (Patrol Torpedo boats). They were mostly built of wood and powered by powerful engines, which made them fast and agile and ideal for hit-and-run attacks under cover of darkness. They carried torpedoes, machine guns, and depth charges, and were often used to ambush enemy ships or support amphibious landings. One of the most well-known PT boat commanders was John F. Kennedy, who commanded PT-109 in the Solomon Islands. In addition to PT boats, the Navy also used submarine chasers (SC boats) and patrol craft (PC boats) for night patrols, particularly for anti-submarine roles. These vessels were equipped with sonar and depth charges and were often used to protect convoys. Destroyer escorts (DEs) also played a role, especially on longer patrols. While larger ships used radar and sonar for night operations, it was the smaller boats that took the risks close to shore.
